transcript.text: Every time I put the oven on it runs for a few minutes and then the trip switch goes and half the house loses power. Reset it 3 times tonight. Hotpoint built-in, about 9 years old. What could cause this?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. The most likely cause is a heating element whose insulation leaks to earth once it gets hot; that commonly allows the oven to run briefly, then trips the RCD and takes out other circuits. Less commonly it is heat-damaged wiring, the supply terminal connection, or the control. It is not a thermostat-type fault when the electrics are tripping. Do not use or reset it again: it needs a qualified appliance engineer to insulation-test the elements and inspect the wiring/terminal connections. Which oven function was selected when it tripped—fan oven, conventional heat or grill? That is useful evidence, although it does not prove that particular element is the failed one.
It was the fan oven function each time. I haven't noticed any burning smell or sparks, and I won't reset the trip again until it's been looked at.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The fan-oven element is now the leading suspect: an element can leak to earth only after it has warmed for a few minutes, which is a very typical RCD-trip pattern. However, fan mode does not prove that element alone, as other elements and shared wiring paths can be involved. It must stay isolated and be checked by a qualified appliance engineer, who can insulation-test the elements and inspect the supply terminals and wiring. No burning smell or sparks is reassuring, but it does not rule out an electrical leakage fault.

candidates: Heating element insulation breaking down and leaking to earth when hot (high)
Damaged oven wiring, terminal connection or control (medium)
